title: Exactness data for the ringed-topos projection mate
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small ringed sites, with sheaves of commutative rings and a ring map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Derived tensor is computed by replacing one factor by a K-flat resolution. Write $L=Lf^*$ for derived extension of scalars after inverse image and $R=Rf_*$ for the derived direct image computed using K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], with their canonical derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to1$. Derived tensor is exact in each variable. The canonical pullback tensor isomorphism
$$\mu_{M,N}:L(M\otimes^L_{R_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes^L_{R_X}LN$$
is natural, unital, and compatible with the canonical integer-shift structures. For every $E\in D(R_X)$, the functors $F(P)=RE\otimes^L_{R_Y}P$ and $G(P)=R(E\otimes^L_{R_X}LP)$ are exact, and the natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ adjoint to $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{RE,P}$ commutes with these shift structures: if $s_F:F(P[1])\cong F(P)[1]$ and $s_G:G(P[1])\cong G(P)[1]$, then
$$s_G\alpha_{P[1]}=\alpha_P[1]s_F.$$
Consequently applying $\alpha$ to a distinguished triangle gives a morphism of distinguished triangles, including its connecting square. These structures are natural in $E$ and $P$; under the tensor-unit identifications $L(R_Y)=R_X$ and $RE\otimes^L R_Y=RE$, one has $\alpha_{R_Y}=1_{RE}$.

Stacks sites-cohomology 0B56 (l.13660-13679) defines the projection map as the adjoint of Lf^*Rf_*E⊗Lf^*K→E⊗Lf^*K. The item's alpha=R(beta)eta_F with beta=(eps_E⊗1)mu_{RE,P} has the same direction, and the coefficients agree: module sheaves over commutative rings, unbounded D. More on Algebra 0FNH gives the (-1)^{pb} sign. There is no SGA citation. Against the item's live version, only proof, proof_deps and split_report changed. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical, and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Re-split note (reopened, 8001 chars, the Q19 cc248 FIX text): the parent is now 3 steps, 1339 chars, and the delivery adds 2 unsplit nodes. Mapping of old steps: old 1 was already a citation step and stays in parent Step 1. Old 2 is now lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit together with the landed total-tensor-integer-shifts leaf. Old 3 is the landed kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated. Old 4-7 are lem-weil-pbc-formal-exact-projection-mate. Every argument therefore has a carrier node. Formal child: I recomputed each clause. Naturality comes from naturality of mu, eps and eta. The shift equation follows from parts (i)-(iii) of commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker, using fixed-input naturality for eps⊗1. The third square holds via the shift equation and naturality at w. The unit equation R(rho_E(1⊗u))alpha_{E,1}=rho_{RE} follows from interchange, naturality of rho, the u-hypothesis, naturality of eta and the triangle identity. It is true; I tested it on the identity adjunction. It is abstract (no ringed sites, no invertibility), so it does not restate the item. Normalization child: c_{u;P,Q} of lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence preserves bidegree, so it commutes with the unsigned first shift and the (-1)^{np} second shift. I checked n=0, n=±1, two odd shifts and characteristic 2. R_Y[0] is K-flat. The action-unitor clauses descend through site-derived-tensor-descent. No flatness of the ring map is used. Its L-shifts are the same ones that derived-adjunction-shift fixes. Duplicate candidates are not duplicates: lem-sc-* projection and pullback shift nodes (proper Noetherian schemes, supplied monoidal structure), lem-trf-adjoint-mate (no tensor), ringed-slice-comparisons-shift (slices only), and lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift (cites the item, so it is downstream). There are no cycles, and both nodes have honest searches. Maintainer note: the formal child carries the largest share (old steps 4-7) and could later be cut into a shift/triangle node and a naturality/unit node. No fixes.
